title: 90 The evaluation of source and level of rumen undegradable protein on growth performance and ovarian parameters in beef heifers developed in dry-lots
content:
Abstract
Heifers supplemented 50% animal sourced rumen undegradable protein (RUP) had increased pregnancy rates compared to heifers supplemented animal sourced 36% RUP, however heifers supplemented plant sourced 36% and 50% RUP had similar growth performance and ovarian development. The effect of source and level of RUP on growth performance and ovarian parameters is unknown. The objective of this study was to evaluate source and level of RUP on growth performance and ovarian parameters in heifers developed in a dry-lot. Crossbred heifers (N = 20) were randomly assigned to one of four RUP supplements: 1) 36% plant sourced RUP (36P, n = 5), 2) 50% plant sourced RUP (50P, n = 5), 3) 36% animal sourced RUP (36A, n = 5), or 4) 50% animal sourced RUP (50A, n = 5). Heifers were individually supplemented once daily for 77 days (d) utilizing Calan Broadbent feeding systems and were offered ad libitum Sudan hay. Heifers were offered supplement at a rate of 1.13 kg/hd/d. Bodyweights (BW) were recorded and blood samples were collected biweekly. Blood samples collected were analyzed for progesterone (P4) concentrations. At the end of the supplementation period heifers underwent bilateral ovariectomies. Weight, length, and height of each ovary was recorded. Surface antral follicles were counted and recorded on each ovary and the length and height of the largest follicle was recorded. Heifer BW and average daily gain (ADG) were analyzed as repeated measures in PROC MIXED. Ovarian and follicular parameters were analyzed utilizing PROC MIXED. Puberty attainment was analyzed using PROC GLIMMIX. Level and source did not influence heifer BW and ADG (P ≥ 0.29). Level × source tended to affect heifer BW with 50A tending to have decreased BW compared to 36A (P = 0.06). Heifer ADG was affected by level × week (P = 0.04) with 36 level heifers having increased ADG compared to 50 level heifers on week 6. Level, source, and their interaction did not impact ovarian weight, length, or height (P ≥ 0.15). Surface antral follicle counts, largest follicle, and puberty attainment were not affected by level, source, or level × source (P ≥ 0.13). In conclusion, level of animal sourced RUP influenced heifer BW with 36A tending to have greater BW increased BW than 50A heifers, but level and source of RUP did not influence ovarian parameters. It is plausible the level and source of RUP is not affecting the ovary but other reproductive tissues. USDA is an equal opportunity provider and employer.
